Professor '''Vyda Kęsgailaitė-Ragulskienė''' (4 June 1931 – 4 January 2009)<ref>[https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/vyda-ragulskiene/ Vyda Ragulskienė biography at VLE]</ref> was a [[Lithuania]]n scientist, inventor, the first woman to become [[Dr.habil.]] of technical sciences in Lithuania.

== Biographical facts ==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2020}}
Ragulskienė was born in the family of Leonas Kęsgaila-Kenstavičius (1895–1979) and Stefanija Stanevičiūtė-Kęsgailienė (1899–1984) in the village of [[Dapšiai]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Netekome prof. Vydos Kęsgailaitės-Ragulskienės|url=http://mokslasplius.lt/mokslo-lietuva/2006-2011/node/1487.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122244/http://mokslasplius.lt/mokslo-lietuva/2006-2011/node/1487.html|archive-date=2016-03-04|access-date=2020-06-12|website=mokslasplius.lt}}</ref> In 1955, she graduated with honour from [[Kaunas Polytechnical Institute]].<ref name="one">{{Cite web|last=VOVERIENĖ|first=Ona|date=|title=Išsaugojusi dvasios aukštį, gaivinanti šaknis|url=http://archyvas.xxiamzius.lt/archyvas/xxiamzius/20020306/zvil_01.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304205320/http://www.xxiamzius.lt/archyvas/xxiamzius/20020306/zvil_01.html|archive-date=2016-03-04|access-date=2020-06-12|website=xxiamzius.lt|language=lt|url-status=live}}</ref> She was a research associate of the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]] (1958–1967). From 1967 to 1993 she worked at Kaunas Polytechnical Institute (later Kaunas University of Technology).<ref name="one" /> While studying in the Kaunas Polytechnical Institute, she graduated from [[Juozas Gruodis Higher Musical School]]<ref name="one" /> (now it is a conservatory).

She was wife of engineer [[Kazimieras Ragulskis]].<ref name="one" />

== Scientific achievements ==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2020}}
In 1965, she defended the dissertation of candidate of technical sciences (doctoral degree).<ref name="one" /> In 1973 she defended the dissertation of doctor of sciences (habilitated doctor), and she received the scientific title of professor in 1977.<ref name="one" /> She coauthored six research monographs, about two hundred research papers and 97 patents.<ref name="one" /> For her research work she was awarded the [[State Prize of the Lithuanian SSR]] in 1983.<ref name="one" /> Ragulskienė was a scientific supervisor or consultant of more than fifty defended dissertations.

Her research revealed and explained new phenomena of non-linear vibro-impact systems. She created systems which operate on the basis of new principles. The professor generalized her investigations in research monographs and research papers. The research work of the professor generalizes the results of experimental, analytic and computer studies on the basis of which new theoretical problems and new applications of vibro-impact mechanisms and devices were solved. On the basis of the results of the investigations a number of original devices of vibro-impact type were created which were recognized as inventions.

== General activities ==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2020}}
Ragulskienė translated from English ''[[Samogitia]]: The Unknown in History'' by American author of esoteric books and convicted con man Charles Pichel (1890–1982), who falsely claimed to be a French nobleman and signed Charles Louis Thourot Pichel.<ref>Yves Drolet, [http://pnaf.us/pdfs/aryan-order-of-america.pdf The Aryan  Order  of America and  the  College of Arms of  Canada 1880-1937 ]{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}, Montréal: Yves Dolet, 2015,  62–65 and 88.</ref> She was active in the collection of data for the encyclopedia ''The Officers of the Lithuanian Armed Forces 1918–1953''.<ref name="one" /> She also prepared materials about the history of her native village of Dapšiai.<ref name="one" /> Many prominent Lithuanian people hailed from this village, including [[Kazimieras Simonavičius]], the creator of the science of artillery and multi-stage rockets.<ref name="one" /> Her family history reaches [[Kęsgailos]] of the 14th century.
